title: Why Are People So Tossed About?
summary: William Branham teaches on the difference between intellectual faith and experiential faith, using the Old Testament manna as a type. He explains that many Christians are tossed about because they only eat the manna that falls daily but have not entered into the inner court where the manna is preserved in the golden pot. True rest and stability come from being hid with Christ in the heart, where the Holy Spirit lives through the believer.

title: God Hath A Provided Way
summary: William Branham preaches on God's provision for healing and salvation, using the example of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate that God prepares a way before making a promise. He encourages believers to accept God's promises with bold faith, as healing and redemption are already provided through Christ's sacrifice.

title: The Junction of Time
summary: William Branham preaches on the concept of 'junctions' in biblical history—moments when God performs miraculous signs and wonders before transitioning to a new dispensation. He argues that the current age is at such a junction, evidenced by the increase of evil and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, and calls believers to recognize the signs and prepare for Christ's return.

title: Fellowship With God Through Reconciliation
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of fellowship with God, emphasizing that true fellowship is restored only through the shed blood of Jesus Christ, not through church membership, education, or human efforts. He contrasts the separation caused by sin with the reconciliation available through Christ's atonement, and calls for a genuine, Holy Ghost revival.

title: The Inter-Veil
summary: William Branham preaches on the hidden life in Christ, emphasizing rest and grace over struggle. He uses the Old Testament tabernacle and the veil as a type of Christ's flesh, urging believers to enter the holiest by faith. He contrasts intellectual faith with heart faith, warning against unbelief and moral compromise.

title: The Junction Time
summary: William Branham speaks about the importance of interdenominational fellowship and the signs of the times, emphasizing that God works in unexpected ways at each junction of history. He shares testimonies from his healing campaigns in Germany and Switzerland, and calls believers to follow the Holy Spirit as instinctively as ducks follow their leader.

title: Inspiration
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of casting down reasoning and following the soul's witness to God's Word, using the story of Elijah and Elisha as a type of Christ and the Church. He emphasizes the need for total commitment to God, preparing a place for the Lord's coming, and the danger of grieving the soul through disobedience.

title: The Supernatural
summary: William Branham speaks on the supernatural nature of God and the importance of living in the atmosphere of God's presence. Using the story of Elisha and Naaman, he emphasizes that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers must abide in Christ to experience His power.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of fellowship, emphasizing that true fellowship with God and among believers is only possible through the shed blood of Jesus Christ. He contrasts this with denominational barriers and human efforts, urging unity and a return to the simple Gospel. Branham also shares personal anecdotes and insights from Scripture, particularly the Book of Job and the Old Testament sacrificial system, to illustrate the necessity of the Blood for reconciliation.

title: Hidden Life With Christ
summary: William Branham teaches on the need for a hidden, consecrated life with Christ, using the Old Testament tabernacle as a type. He contrasts the manna in the outer court, which perishes, with the manna in the holiest of holies, which remains fresh, illustrating the difference between a superficial faith and a deep, abiding relationship with God.

title: When Love Is Projected
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of divine love and sovereign grace, sharing testimonies of healing and deliverance. He emphasizes that when human efforts fail and love is projected, God's grace steps in to perform miracles.

title: The Worst Sinner in the City
summary: William Branham preaches on the Pharisee's banquet where Jesus was invited but neglected, drawing parallels to modern churches that invite Christ but fail to honor Him. He contrasts the Pharisee's hypocrisy with the repentant harlot who anoints Jesus' feet, emphasizing that the worst sinner is the one who rejects Christ's love and forgiveness.
themes: God's grace for the worst sinners

title: God's Covenant With Abraham And His Seed
summary: William Branham teaches on God's unconditional covenant with Abraham, emphasizing that God's promises are based on His own will and faithfulness, not human effort. He contrasts faith with knowledge, explains election and foreknowledge, and encourages believers to trust God's Word absolutely for salvation and healing.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the compound redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, emphasizing that God is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses the account of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate faith and God's provision, and draws parallels between Old Testament types and New Testament truths, urging believers to live a fully surrendered life in the Shekinah Glory.

title: Making A Way
summary: William Branham speaks on God's provision of a way of escape in every trial, using biblical examples from Noah, Daniel, Jonah, and the scapegoat. He emphasizes that faith must be anchored in God's eternal Word and the finished work of Christ at Calvary.

title: The True and False Vines
summary: William Branham preaches on the true and false vines, using the Old Testament types of Cain and Abel, Jacob and Esau, and Israel and Moab to illustrate the difference between true and false worship. He emphasizes that mere religious profession is not enough; one must be born again and have the Spirit of God.

title: God Using His Gift
summary: William Branham speaks on how God uses His gift through believers' faith, using the story of Blind Bartimaeus to illustrate that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He emphasizes that miracles are not past but present, and that faith can touch God today just as it did in biblical times.
themes: the gift of the Holy Spirit

title: Easter Sunrise
subtitle: 56-0401S
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that because He lives, believers shall live also. He reflects on the sorrow of Mary and Martha at the tomb, the rejection and death of Christ, and the triumph of His resurrection. Branham encourages the congregation to have the blessed hope of resurrection and eternal life, and announces that Jesus is alive and present among them.

title: The Mighty Conqueror
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham emphasizes the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the central proof of His divinity and the foundation of Christian faith. He recounts personal testimonies of healings and miracles to demonstrate that Christ is alive and active today, just as He was in the Gospels. Branham urges believers to trust solely in Christ, not in denominations or human wisdom, and to recognize His presence in their daily lives.

title: Shepherd of the Sheepfold
summary: William Branham shares his recent experiences in Mexico, including a miraculous healing of a dead baby and a large altar call. He reflects on the relationship between the shepherd and the sheep, emphasizing God's care and the helplessness of humanity without Christ.

title: The Infallibility of God's Spoken Word
summary: William Branham teaches on the absolute perfection and unchangeable nature of God's spoken Word. He explains that once God speaks a promise, He is bound to fulfill it because He is infallible and cannot contradict Himself. Using examples from the Old Testament, Branham illustrates how God always makes a way to keep His Word, whether through the ark for Noah, the fiery furnace for Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, or the ladder to heaven for Jacob.

title: The Resurrection of Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Jesus, emphasizing that Christ is alive today through the Holy Spirit and continues His ministry among believers. He uses the account of the disciples on the road to Emmaus to illustrate how Jesus reveals Himself through Scripture and familiar actions, and he encourages the congregation to recognize Christ's presence and power in their midst.
themes: Presence of Christ through the Holy Spirit

title: The Infallible Word of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the absolute reliability and divine authority of the Bible as God's infallible Word. He uses the analogy of a bridge builder who tests every material to illustrate how God has time-tested His Word and provided Jesus Christ as the only bridge between humanity and God. Branham calls listeners to build their faith solely on Scripture, warning against false signs and doctrines that deviate from the finished work of Christ.
themes: Testing of spirits by the Word

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith in Jesus Christ as the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to trust God's Word and power for healing and salvation, despite criticism and unbelief.

title: What Is A Vision?
summary: William Branham explains the nature of visions, describing them as material and real experiences given by God. He shares personal accounts of visions and discusses the operation of the Holy Spirit in healing ministry, emphasizing that the gift is for God's glory and not for public show.

title: The Time Is At Hand
summary: William Branham preaches on the urgency of the present time as the fulfillment of biblical prophecy, emphasizing that the end times are near and calling for decision for Christ. He highlights the universal revival and signs of the times, urging healing and salvation.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that faith in Him can bring healing and salvation. He encourages the congregation to trust in God's provision and to keep their promises to Him.

title: The Deep Calling to the Deep
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of 'the deep calling to the deep,' using examples from nature and Scripture to illustrate how God's Spirit calls to the human spirit. He emphasizes that God always has a witness on earth and that believers should trust in God's promises, as exemplified by Simeon who was promised to see the Christ before his death.

title: Earnestly Contending For The Faith That Was Once Delivered Unto The Saints
summary: William Branham explains the nature of divine healing, emphasizing that healing comes from God through faith, not from any human healer. He urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, which includes the same works and signs that Jesus performed, such as healing the sick and discerning thoughts. Branham contrasts true faith with denominational traditions and calls for a return to the apostolic faith.
themes: the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: When Their Eyes Were Opened
summary: William Branham speaks on the resurrection of Jesus Christ and the need for believers to recognize His living presence today. He emphasizes that the same works Jesus performed on earth, such as healing and discerning thoughts, are still available through the Holy Spirit. Branham encourages the audience to shut out distractions and invite Christ into their hearts to experience His power.
themes: Divine healing as earnest of resurrection
Rejection of Christ's works as blasphemy

title: What Visions Are
summary: William Branham explains the nature of visions as divine revelations from God, using biblical examples and personal experiences to illustrate how visions operate and how faith interacts with healing. He emphasizes the importance of believing God's Word and the role of visions in his ministry.
themes: the role of the Holy Spirit

title: Show Us The Father And It'll Satisfy
summary: William Branham speaks on seeing God through His universe, His Word, His Son, and His people. He emphasizes that God reveals Himself in nature and that faith is required to perceive Him. The sermon includes personal anecdotes and a call to recognize God's presence in all things.
themes: the Father revealed in the Son

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He urges believers to seek a simple, faith-based relationship with Jesus rather than relying on education or denominational doctrines, and highlights that the same works Christ did should be evident in His church today.
themes: Holy Spirit's work in the church

title: Faith
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of faith, using the story of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate unwavering trust in God's promises. He emphasizes that God's redemptive names, such as Jehovah-jireh, are unchanging and that believers should rest in God's Word rather than be swayed by circumstances or feelings.

title: God's Covenant With Abraham
summary: William Branham speaks on the covenant God made with Abraham, emphasizing the importance of unwavering faith in God's promises regardless of circumstances. He encourages believers to look to God's Word rather than symptoms, and illustrates this with stories of healing and faith.

title: Teaching on Moses
summary: William Branham speaks on Mother's Day, addressing mothers and children. He uses the story of Moses' parents, Amram and Jochebed, to illustrate faith and prayer under oppression, emphasizing the value of the soul and the importance of losing one's life for Christ.

title: At Kadesh-Barnea
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament account of Israel at Kadesh-Barnea, using it as a type for the modern church. He warns against the 'mixed multitude' of nominal believers and calls for a genuine, born-again faith that stands firm under trial.
themes: The mixed multitude in the church
The need for a born-again experience
Judgment beginning at the house of God

title: The Lamb's Book of Life
summary: William Branham teaches on the value of souls over material wealth, using personal anecdotes and biblical references. He explores the concept of perfection through Christ, the shadow of the law, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit, urging believers to separate from the world and win souls.

title: Perfection
summary: William Branham discusses the concept of perfection through the lens of Hebrews 10, explaining how the law was a shadow of good things to come and how Christ's sacrifice provides true purification. He emphasizes that only through the blood of Christ can a worshipper be purged of sin and have no more conscience of sin.

title: Life Is The Healer
summary: William Branham teaches that life itself is the healer, not medicine, and that healing was already purchased at Calvary. He contrasts faith in God with reliance on medical science, explaining that sickness is a devil that must be cast out, and that true healing comes from the life of God within.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham and the covenant name Jehovah-Jireh, emphasizing God's sovereign grace and the believer's inheritance of all redemptive promises through Christ. He calls for separation from the world and trust in God's Word despite circumstances.

title: God Provided a Lamb
summary: William Branham preaches on Abraham's faith and God's covenant, emphasizing that believers are Abraham's seed and heirs of the promise. He discusses divine healing as part of the atonement, the importance of love over gifts, and the need for a faith that goes beyond intellectual assent to a deep soul experience.

title: An Exodus
summary: William Branham preaches on the Exodus of the Israelites from Egypt as a type of the church's calling out from the world. He emphasizes the need for a genuine experience with God, the power of faith over circumstances, and the importance of being filled with the Holy Spirit.

title: Revelation, Book of Symbols
summary: William Branham speaks on the Book of Revelation as a book of symbols, emphasizing that God hides truth from the wise and reveals it to babes. He discusses election, the love of God, and the importance of the new birth over theological knowledge. He also shares testimonies of healing and the need for the Church to receive the revelation of Jesus Christ in the last days.

title: The Law Having a Shadow
summary: William Branham teaches from Hebrews 10 about the law being a shadow of good things to come, emphasizing that the Old Testament law foreshadowed Christ. He explains that the law could not make worshippers perfect, but Christ's sacrifice perfects believers forever through the Holy Spirit. Branham also shares testimonies of healings and discusses the importance of faith in God's Word.

title: The Mark Of The Beast
summary: William Branham preaches on the mark of the beast, emphasizing that it begins with rejecting the Gospel and sealing one's ears to the truth. He uses Old Testament types like the jubilee year and the boring of the slave's ear to illustrate how refusal to accept Christ's liberation leads to spiritual bondage. Branham warns against worldliness, particularly in dress and behavior, as evidence of the antichrist spirit.

title: All Things Are Possible To Him That Believeth
summary: William Branham preaches on Mark 9:23, emphasizing that all things are possible to those who believe. He discusses the relationship between faith and healing, arguing that divine healing is included in the atonement. He uses the story of the epileptic boy to illustrate how doubt and unbelief hinder God's power, and encourages believers to have simple faith in God's Word.

title: Led by the Spirit of God
summary: William Branham preaches on being led by the Spirit of God, emphasizing that true believers walk not after the flesh but after the Spirit. He discusses the proper use of spiritual gifts, the necessity of the Holy Spirit baptism, and the importance of separating from worldly influences.

title: Love
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of divine love, emphasizing that love is the greatest force and that when human love reaches its limit, sovereign grace takes over. He shares personal stories and biblical examples to illustrate that genuine love for God transforms a person and is the true evidence of the Holy Spirit.

title: Making the Valley Full of Ditches
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for genuine, Holy Ghost-filled Christianity, contrasting it with lukewarm, borderline belief. Using the story of Elisha and the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom, he emphasizes the importance of being separated from the world and filled with the Spirit to receive God's provision.

title: Raising Jairus' Daughter
summary: William Branham preaches on the raising of Jairus' daughter, emphasizing Jesus' compassion and power over death. He encourages faith in Christ's resurrection and His ability to heal and save today.

title: The Church And Its Condition
summary: William Branham preaches on the condition of the church, using the symbolism of the lamb and the dove to illustrate the need for meekness, gentleness, and submission to the Holy Spirit. He contrasts the nature of a true Christian with that of a hypocrite, and calls for a return to sacrificial living and holiness.

title: Divine Love and Sovereign Grace
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of divine love as the foundation for all spiritual gifts, using the Exodus account of Israel at the Red Sea to illustrate how love projected toward God brings sovereign grace into action. He emphasizes that love casts out fear and that when human effort ends, God's grace takes over.

title: Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of faith, using Abraham as the prime example. He emphasizes that true faith holds to God's promise regardless of circumstances, and that believers must separate from unbelievers and ignore symptoms. He encourages the congregation to call those things which are not as though they were, because God said so.

title: The Working of the Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on the operation of the Holy Spirit in his ministry, using the analogy of a carnival knothole to explain how the gift of God works through him. He emphasizes that it is the faith of the people that draws from the gift, and shares a vision of healing in Denver to illustrate God's direct intervention. The sermon also covers the covenant with Abraham and the role of the Holy Spirit in the Church.
themes: The role of the Holy Spirit

title: Divine Love
summary: William Branham speaks on the nature of divine love and how it leads to sovereign grace. He shares personal testimonies of healing and protection, emphasizing that when human efforts fail, God's grace takes over through love.

title: The Handwriting On The Wall
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Belshazzar's feast and the handwriting on the wall, drawing parallels to the moral and spiritual decline of modern society. He urges believers to purpose in their hearts to serve God faithfully despite worldly pressures, and warns of impending judgment for those who reject God's Word.

title: Azusa Jubilee
summary: William Branham speaks at the Azusa Street Jubilee celebration at Angelus Temple, calling for a return to the old-fashioned Pentecostal experience and a rededication to the Holy Spirit. He uses the Old Testament year of jubilee as a type of spiritual freedom, urging believers to break free from captivity to worldliness and denominational barriers.

title: The Lamb and the Dove
summary: William Branham preaches on the symbolism of the Lamb and the Dove, representing Christ and the Holy Spirit. He emphasizes the need for believers to have a lamb-like nature of meekness and surrender to allow the Holy Spirit (the Dove) to abide in them. He calls for a return to the humility and holiness of the early Pentecostal Azusa Street revival.

title: Spiritual Adoption
summary: William Branham speaks on the concept of spiritual adoption, using the Transfiguration as a backdrop to discuss how believers are adopted as sons of God through Christ. He emphasizes the role of the Holy Spirit as a tutor, training believers to be obedient children, and the importance of revelation in building the Church.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the Mount of Transfiguration, emphasizing that the Church is built upon the revelation of Jesus Christ, not on denominations, laws, or works. He calls believers to hear Jesus alone, who is the only way to salvation, healing, and eternal life.

title: Witnesses
location: Chicago, Illinois (Lane Tech High School auditorium)
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical call for believers to be witnesses of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that a true witness must have a personal encounter with God. He recounts examples from Scripture—Noah, Daniel, the Hebrew children, Moses, Joshua, John the Baptist, and the apostles—and modern testimonies of healing and transformation, urging the audience to take their stand for Christ.

title: The Ministry Explained
summary: William Branham explains the biblical basis for spiritual gifts and divine healing, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He contrasts the faith of the queen of Sheba and the Ninevites with the unbelief of the religious leaders of his day, urging listeners to come and see for themselves.
themes: Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
The Messianic sign of the prophet
The role of spiritual gifts in the Church
The queen of Sheba as a example of seeking God

title: Father, The Hour Has Come
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for the church to return to the old landmarks of the Bible, using the story of Jehoshaphat and Ahab as a warning against compromise and worldliness. He calls for unity, holiness, and a stand on God's Word, emphasizing that true faith is based on revelation and the Blood of Christ, not on human wisdom or denominational pride.

title: Elisha The Prophet
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament prophet Elisha, focusing on the Shunammite woman who built a room for Elisha and was rewarded with a son. He draws parallels between Elisha's double portion of Elijah's spirit and the Church's reception of the Holy Spirit, emphasizing the importance of respecting God's servants and the power of faith.

title: Painted-Face Jezebel
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Jezebel from 2 Kings 9, using her as an example of sin and worldliness that has infiltrated the modern church. He condemns practices such as face painting, hair cutting, and worldly music, calling for a return to holiness and the Holy Spirit.

title: A Wedding Supper
summary: William Branham preaches on the parable of the wedding supper from Matthew 22, emphasizing that God has prepared everything for salvation and healing, and that the Holy Ghost is the robe provided for all who accept the invitation. He calls for repentance and a return to the power of Pentecost.
themes: the robe of the Holy Ghost

title: A Secondhanded Robe
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elijah and Elisha, emphasizing the need for a fresh, firsthand anointing from God rather than relying on secondhand religious experiences or robes. He encourages believers to keep their eyes on God's promises and to seek the power of the God of Elijah for their lives and ministries.

title: A Blushing Prophet
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for repentance and revival, using the biblical example of Ezra who blushed before God for the sins of Israel. He condemns the moral decay and worldliness in the church, calling for a return to holiness and a Holy Ghost revival.

title: A Secondhanded Robe
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Elisha receiving Elijah's mantle, emphasizing the need for a personal relationship with God rather than relying on denominational robes or secondhand faith. He calls for a purging of worldly influences and a sincere pursuit of the Holy Spirit's power.

title: Gifts
summary: William Branham speaks on spiritual gifts, emphasizing that they are rays from the same Spirit of God. He uses the type of Joseph and Moses to illustrate Christ, and explains that Jesus did nothing until the Father showed Him, as seen in the raising of Lazarus. He encourages faith in God's promises regardless of circumstances.
themes: Christ as fulfillment of Old Testament types

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham, emphasizing God's unconditional covenant and the importance of separation from the world. He encourages believers to claim God's promises, including healing, by faith, and demonstrates the power of God's Word through the example of Abraham's unwavering belief.

title: God Making His Promise
summary: William Branham preaches on God's faithfulness to His promises, using the biblical imagery of the Lamb and the Dove to illustrate the nature of Christ and the Holy Spirit. He challenges believers to examine their lives, repent of worldliness, and return to a genuine, holy walk with God.
themes: The nature of Christ as the Lamb
The Holy Spirit as a Dove
Holiness and separation from the world
The unity of the Dove and the Lamb

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on God's covenant with Abraham, focusing on the name Jehovah-Jireh and the finished work of Christ. He emphasizes faith in God's promises, divine healing in the atonement, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Christ, emphasizing that Jesus is the final authority and that believers should 'hear ye Him.' He discusses the finished work of Christ, the relationship between sin and unbelief, and the importance of faith in receiving healing and salvation.

title: Joseph Meeting His Brethren
summary: William Branham teaches on the biblical account of Joseph meeting his brethren, drawing parallels to the life of Jesus Christ and the ongoing conflict between the righteous and evil seeds. He emphasizes the importance of divine revelation and the supernatural vindication of God's chosen people.
